fields.meta_title: Fitness Quiz: Take One or Build Your Own | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take a free fitness quiz that names your workout style, then build one for your gym or class that saves every answer. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Fitness Quiz That Turns Answers Into a Starting Routine
fields.hero_description: Build a fitness quiz that matches each person to a workout style and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Fitness Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: One prompt gives you the quiz and the table of answers behind it. Describe a change, and Emergent makes it.
fields.feature_1:
Every option mapped to a result

Name the workout styles you want as results, such as Strength or Mobility. Emergent writes questions about daily habits and maps each option to one style. Reword any by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Right answers scored, misses explained

For a knowledge quiz, the app marks one correct option per question, adds up each score, and shows a short explanation under every miss. Scores can be split by class period or group.
fields.feature_3:
Class suggestions from your calendar

Connect your class calendar or booking tool through its API. The result screen then lists the upcoming classes tagged with that style, and a new member leaves with a class to try.
fields.feature_4:
An alert for the coach of that style

When someone finishes, the coach who leads their style gets an email or Slack alert with the result and every answer. Pick a different coach for each style in your prompt.
fields.feature_5:
One question per screen, no response cap

People answer one question per screen with a progress bar, which suits a phone at the front desk. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and a January signup rush records every result.
fields.feature_6:
Your own domain and full code export

Host the quiz on your gym's own domain, included with Emergent and paid in credits. Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans and keep building it there.

fields.usecase_heading: A Gym, a Class, an App, and a Rec Center
fields.tab_content_1:
Jonah gets 3 classes to try from a Strength result

Harbor Iron Gym puts the fitness quiz on its join page. Jonah Whitcombe finishes with Strength, and the result screen lists the 3 beginner strength classes on this week's calendar, pulled through the calendar's API. His result goes to the member table, and coach Mateo Lund gets an email with every answer.
fields.tab_content_2:
Period 4 gets heart rate retaught by Monday

Coach Ingrid Salo gives her 8th graders a 10-question fitness knowledge quiz on heart rate and muscle groups. The app scores each student and counts misses by period. In period 4, 9 of 27 students missed the target heart rate question, against 4 or fewer in every other period, and she reteaches it Monday.
fields.tab_content_3:
Rafael opens the app to a week of mobility work

Fennwick asks new users 6 questions at signup, before it shows a single workout. Rafael Ambrose answers on his phone and lands on Mobility. The app saves the result to his profile and opens his first week with 3 mobility sessions of 20 minutes each, then asks one check-in question after session 3.
fields.tab_content_4:
2 strength classes added for spring after 1,240 results

All winter, the quiz ran on a lobby tablet and the website at Alder Point Rec Center, and 1,240 people finished it. Strength led with 410 results, then Cardio with 360, Mobility with 290, and Sport with 180. The program director added 2 evening strength classes to the spring schedule.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Fitness Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a fitness quiz that sorts people by workout style or scores what they know, with every result tested.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write the styles before the questions
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask about habits, not fitness levels
fields.howto_step_1_des: Settle this first, because it changes every question. A knowledge quiz for a class marks answers right or wrong and adds up a score. A gym or app quiz matches habits to a workout style, and each option points to a result instead.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each result a name, two sentences on what the style looks like, and a few classes or sessions to start with. Four styles, such as Strength, Cardio, Mobility, and Sport, leave room for every option to land somewhere.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask what people do and enjoy: how they spend a free Saturday, or which class they would pick first. Skip questions that ask people to rate how fit they are, and save injuries and health history for a conversation with a coach.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For a knowledge quiz, take each answer from a published guideline, such as the CDC's physical activity guidelines for adults. Show a one-line explanation with the source under each question, and students learn the fact from the miss as well as the score.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Hold a matching quiz to 8 questions
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put one question on each screen with a progress bar, and keep a matching quiz near 8 questions. Before you share it, take it on a phone and time yourself. If it runs past 3 minutes, cut the weakest question.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Give each result one next step
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide what a person can do the moment the result appears: book a first class, start a week of sessions, or hear from the coach who leads that style. Put that step in your prompt, and Emergent builds it along with the quiz.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run through the quiz four times, once aiming at each style, and confirm the right result appears every time. For a scored quiz, miss every question on purpose once and read each explanation. Then open the saved rows.

faq_plan.a: A fitness quiz is a short set of questions that either tests what someone knows about exercise or matches their habits to a style of workout. The quiz on this page asks 8 questions and names one of 4 styles: Strength, Cardio, Mobility, or Sport.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a fitness quiz?
faq_plan.a: Decide whether it scores answers or matches them to workout styles, then describe the results and what follows each one in a prompt. Emergent's AI survey builder drafts the quiz and the table that stores every finished quiz. Test each result, then publish the link.

faq_plan.q: Can you give me some quiz questions about fitness?
faq_plan.ref: Can you give me some quiz questions about fitness?

prov.original: Can you give me some quiz questions about fitness?

faq_plan.a: Yes. For a knowledge round, ask how many minutes of moderate-intensity activity adults need each week: the CDC says at least 150 minutes. Ask how many days of muscle-strengthening activity adults need: the CDC says 2. For a matching quiz, ask how someone would spend a free Saturday morning, or which class they would try first.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free fitness quiz I can take right now?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The free fitness quiz on this page asks for no account or email. Answer 8 questions, and it names the workout style your picks lean toward, with places to start. For a result about clothes instead of workouts, take the style quiz. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing your own.

faq_plan.q: How do I write fitness quiz questions and answers that stay accurate?
faq_plan.a: Base each answer on a published guideline instead of memory, and quote it in the explanation under the question. Recheck the guideline before each new school year or season. Keep answers to numbers and facts the guideline states, and leave weight-loss and diet tips out of the quiz.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a fitness quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Eight works well for a matching quiz with 4 styles: every question offers one option per style, and each style gets 8 chances to score. A scored class quiz can run to 10 questions at one point each, and the total reads as a mark out of 10.

faq_plan.q: Can a fitness quiz use yes or no questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for simple habit checks such as whether someone trains at least twice a week. A yes or no answer splits people into only two groups. Pair it with multiple-choice questions when the quiz names one of 4 styles. For a check-in where every answer is Yes or No, build a yes no questions survey instead.

faq_plan.q: How can a gym use a fitness quiz on its join page?
faq_plan.a: Put it on the join page and show each result with a few beginner classes that match it. Save each result to the member record, and the first coach a new member meets already knows their style. On Emergent, those records sit in a database the gym owns.

faq_plan.q: How do I find which fitness quiz questions a class missed most?
faq_plan.a: Count misses for each question, split by class period, instead of looking only at each student's total. A question that a third of one period misses points to the lesson, not the students. On Emergent, the answers sit in a database you own, ready to sort by period and question.

faq_plan.q: Can a fitness quiz give a score instead of a workout style?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A knowledge version marks one option right per question, totals the score, and shows an explanation after each miss. It scores the same way a vocabulary quiz does, only the answers come from activity guidelines instead of a dictionary.

quiz.title: Your Fitness Style in 8 Questions
quiz.intro: Eight questions about how you like to move. Your result names the workout style your answers lean toward, with a few places to start.

questions.text: You have a free Saturday morning. What sounds best?

options.text: Lifting at the gym before it gets busy
A long run or bike ride outside
A slow yoga class with lots of stretching
A pickup game of basketball or soccer

questions.text: Which piece of equipment would you grab first?

options.text: A pair of dumbbells
A jump rope
A foam roller
A ball

questions.text: What kind of progress would feel best after a month?

options.text: Lifting heavier than you did on day one
Going farther before you need a break
Touching your toes without bending your knees
Winning more points in your weekly game

questions.text: How long would you like a workout to last?

options.text: About 45 minutes with rests between sets
An hour or more at a steady pace
Around 20 minutes, done most days
However long the game runs

questions.text: Which class would you sign up for?

options.text: Barbell basics
Indoor cycling
Pilates or stretching
A rec league volleyball team

questions.text: What keeps you coming back to a workout?

options.text: Writing down a new personal best
Music and a rhythm you can settle into
Feeling loose and calm afterward
Teammates who expect you to show up
The weight room
A trail or a track
A quiet studio or your living room
A court or a field

questions.text: Pick a goal for the next season.

options.text: Learn to deadlift with good form
Finish a 5K without stopping
Hold a full squat with heels down
Make the playoffs with your team

results.title: Strength
results.description: Your answers lean toward lifting and clear, measurable progress. Start with a beginner barbell or dumbbell class two days a week, and write down each lift so you can see it climb. A coach can check your form in the first few sessions.

results.title: Cardio
results.description: Your answers lean toward steady, longer efforts like running, cycling, or rowing. Pick one and build up the time you spend on it each week. A group ride or a local running club gives the week a fixed time to show up.

results.title: Mobility
results.description: Your answers lean toward slow, controlled movement and feeling loose afterward. Try a yoga, Pilates, or stretching class, or 20 minutes at home on most days. Hips, shoulders, and the upper back are good places to start.

results.title: Sport
results.description: Your answers lean toward games, teammates, and a score at the end. Look for a rec league, a pickup game, or a club team that plays weekly. Short drills between games, such as sprints or footwork, keep you sharp for the next one.

plan.angle: Searchers want a fitness quiz to take and quiz questions to use. The page gives both: an 8-question quiz that names a workout style (Strength, Cardio, Mobility, or Sport), sample knowledge questions with sourced answers, and four businesses that act on results: a gym join page, a middle school PE class scored by period, a workout app that sets a first week, and a rec center that plans its schedule from the count. Every answer lands in a database the owner keeps.
